conversation:
incident-bot: [PAGER] HIGH GPU UTILIZATION  dedicated pool `novara-prod` (tenant: Novara Health). GPUs at 96% across pool, request queueing increasing, 5xx spikes on inference endpoints.

oncall-sre: Ack. I'm oncall and taking. Pulling pool and node logs now.

eng-runtime-lead: Joining. Any autoscale activity or host errors showing? 

oncall-sre: Autoscaler attempted scale but failed: region host quota temporarily exhausted due to control-plane maintenance. Pool is single-tenant reserved (Novara) and they're using ~92% of their reserved sessions. A few keys show sustained long-context (>1200 tokens) churn.

se-rosa: Novara's contract: reserved 12 GPUs, burst allowance +2 (short) if ops approves. I'll ping Novara SRE.

acct-mgr-jim: Confirmed: burst allowed but billable. Need ops/governance approval. I'll prep a billing note.

eng-runtime-lead: Options:
- A) Trigger emergency burst (+2 GPUs) to reduce immediate queueing (fast)
- B) Apply per-key short token cap (700 tokens) on heavy routes and opt-in model-fallback to quantized variant `gptx-q8` for long requests (some quality loss)
- C) Evict low-priority tenants from sibling pools and attempt rebalancing (slower, noisy)

oncall-sre: I recommend A+B: burst to bring error rate down, and soft token cap + canary fallback (10%) to `gptx-q8` for top offending route to limit further tail pressure.

eng-runtime-lead: Agreed. I'll request ops burst and patch route policy.

ops-bot: Executing API call:
```
POST /internal/pools/novara-prod/burst
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
{
  "enable": true,
  "requested_gpus": 2,
  "ttl_minutes": 20,
  "reason": "emergency - tenant spike Novara"
}
```

ops-bot: 202 Accepted  Provisioning queued (~70s). burst_id: brst-nv4k

oncall-sre: Applying route policy for `/v1/novara/infer/long`:
```
throttle_per_key: 20 rpm
max_request_tokens: 700
fallback_variant: gptx-q8
canary_pct: 10
note: "temporary - reduce queueing"
```

eng-runtime-lead: Burst came up. Initial GPU usage dropping 96% -> 74% within 90s. 5xx rate falling.

novara-sre: (via se-rosa) "We inadvertently started a bulk embeddings migration across prod keys; pausing now. Thanks for the rapid response."

oncall-sre: Monitoring: queue depth down 55%, 5xx errors back to baseline. Latency tail improved but still slightly elevated for long requests.

acct-mgr-jim: Notified Novara about burst being billable. Created internal charge ticket NOV-CHG-482.

eng-runtime-lead: Keep burst for 20 minutes while traffic decays. If Novara pauses job and metrics normalize, we'll drain and remove route caps. If not, propose increasing reserved capacity or scheduled burst windows.

customer-succ: Novara confirms pause. They request ETA to full restoration and want a post-incident note.

oncall-sre: ETA: We'll keep throttles/fallback until burst drains and metrics stable for 10 continuous minutes. Expect ~25-30 minutes total. We'll send a postmortem with timeline and suggested customer runbook.

10m-check - oncall-sre: Metrics stable, no 5xx in last 8 minutes. Queue depth trending to normal.

eng-runtime-lead: Preparing controlled drain in 10m. Will remove canary fallback after traffic normalizes.

ops-bot: Executing burst rollback:
```
POST /internal/pools/novara-prod/burst/stop
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
{
  "burst_id": "brst-nv4k",
  "drain_timeout_seconds": 120
}
```

ops-bot: 200 OK  Burst drained, GPUs deprovisioned. Pool steady ~38%.

oncall-sre: Removing temporary route policy now.

oncall-sre: Patch removed for `/v1/novara/infer/long`: throttles off, fallback_variant cleared.

eng-runtime-lead: Created incident ticket INC-2026-1767565432 (Severity: Sev2) with action items: measure per-key long-context usage, proposal for scheduled burst windows, consider upgrading Novara reserved capacity or formal pre-approved burst scheduling.

acct-mgr-jim: Billing notification sent to Novara with estimated minutes and cost. Customer acknowledged.

se-rosa: Novara asks for guidance: they will shift bulk migrations to off-peak and will request scheduled burst windows for future runs.

oncall-sre: Recommend follow-up automations:
- early soft alerts when single tenant >70% sustained for 10m
- auto-offer scheduled burst window via console
- automated model-fallback policy triggered by queue depth thresholds (non-silent to customer)

oncall-sre: Handoff: I'm wrapping up. If anything reoccurs, page #incidents and the SRE oncall rota. Closing incident: resolved.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: INC-2026-1767565432  status: resolved.
